title: Acyclicity and projection equations for a restricted varying-ring resolution
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ a sequence of sheaves of commutative rings, and $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings with compatible homomorphisms $A\to B_n$. Let $\mathscr S(B)$ be the category of strict semilinear module systems, identified with modules over $B$ on the sequence site $\mathcal T=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$, with componentwise exactness [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and write $[K]$ for the derived object of a complex and $[f]$ for the class of a chain map [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $U_0N=(\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B_n}N_n)_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $g$ be the sequence-site projection with constant inverse image, put $\Delta A=g^{-1}A$, let $r:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T),\Delta A)$ be the identity on underlying topoi with structural map $\Delta A\to B$, and put $p=g\circ r$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Under the sequence-site identification, $r_*=U_0$ is exact and $g_*=\lim$, computed degreewise on complexes. For every K-injective system resolution $a:N\to I$ and every K-injective tower resolution $j:U_0I\to J$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], the chain map $\lim j:\lim U_0I\to\lim J$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The ordinary complex $p_*I$ is canonically $\lim U_0I$. For each $n$, both $U_0a_n$ and $j_n$ are quasi-isomorphisms, and the following equality holds in $D(A)$:
$$[U_0a_n]^{-1}[j_n]^{-1}[\operatorname{pr}_n^J][\lim j]=[U_0a_n]^{-1}[\operatorname{pr}_n^{U_0I}].$$
Here $\operatorname{pr}_n$ denotes the degreewise inverse-limit projection; $U_0a_n$ means scalar restriction of $a_n$. These identifications commute with the canonical derived resolution transitions in $a,j$. There is no assumption that $U_0I$ or any $I_n$ is K-injective.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), applied to identity-topos ring restriction followed by the sequence-site projection of section-derived-limits; agent records the two-resolution projection equation.

proof.text: Under the sequence-site identification in the hypotheses, $r$ is the coefficient-change morphism for $\Delta A\to B$: its direct image is restriction of scalars. On underlying abelian sheaves this changes neither sections nor maps; componentwise exactness therefore makes $r_*=U_0$ exact. The direct image of $g$ is the tower limit stipulated in the statement. Explicitly, a section of $g_*r_*M$ over $V$ is a family $(x_n)$, $x_n\in M_n(V)$, compatible with all transitions. Its $A(V)$-action is the componentwise action through $A(V)\to B_n(V)$. This is exactly $\lim U_0M$, including its projection maps. Applying the description in every complex degree gives $p_*I=g_*r_*I=\lim U_0I$.

Use the resolving-adjunction comparison isIso_map_of_adjoints underlying the normalized ringed-topos composition theorem. Construct the left adjoint of U0 by extending scalars at each level, with transition b tensor x sent to image(b) tensor transition(x); the normalized scalar adjunctions give its adjunction to U0. Constant towers are left adjoint to inverse limit. Resolve a tower by viewing it as a strict system over the constant ring A and taking the existing sequence-site K-flat resolution. Exact restriction along identities identifies the resulting componentwise K-flat tower with a resolution of the original tower. Scalar extension inverts quasi-isomorphisms between these representatives, by the scalar model at each level. Constant towers preserve K-flatness and quasi-isomorphisms. The generic comparison theorem, with the K-injective Hom bijections at I and J, therefore makes the localized map lim j invertible, hence lim j is a quasi-isomorphism. This proves the given acyclicity assertion for independent site and coefficient universes, without assuming U0I is K-injective.

A K-injective resolution is a quasi-isomorphism by definition. Since exactness of $\mathscr S(B)$ is componentwise, kernels, images and hence cohomology of a system complex are componentwise. Thus $a_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Scalar restriction keeps the underlying abelian complex, its cycles, boundaries and cohomology; consequently $U_0a_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism as well. For the tower resolution $j$, exactness of tower evaluation gives the same conclusion for $j_n$. This proves that both inverses occurring in the asserted equation exist in $D(A)$; it makes no assertion about K-injectivity of $I_n$.

Naturality of the ordinary limit-cone projections gives an equality of chain maps $\operatorname{pr}_n^J\circ\lim j=j_n\circ\operatorname{pr}_n^{U_0I}$. Take classes in $D(A)$ and compose on the left first with $[j_n]^{-1}$ and then with $[U_0a_n]^{-1}$. Cancellation gives exactly $[U_0a_n]^{-1}[j_n]^{-1}[\operatorname{pr}_n^J][\lim j]=[U_0a_n]^{-1}[\operatorname{pr}_n^{U_0I}]$.

Precomposition by a quasi-isomorphism is bijective on homotopy classes of maps into a K-injective target. Apply this to a with target I-prime to obtain k and a homotopy ak to a-prime, then to j with target J-prime to obtain l and a homotopy jl to (U0k)j-prime. The same injectivity proves uniqueness of both comparison classes. Localizing the homotopies and canceling a and j gives the displayed fractions. The fractions imply that k and l are quasi-isomorphisms. Quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives are homotopy equivalences, so additive restriction and inverse limit preserve them and their homotopy inverses. Applying inverse limit to the second homotopy and localizing gives the comparison square. The fractions and uniqueness characterize the canonical derived resolution transitions; the definition of directImageComplexIso is the identity identification with the composite functor.

For the projections, evaluation of $lj\simeq j'U_0k$ gives $[j_n']^{-1}[l_n]=[U_0k_n][j_n]^{-1}$, while $ka\simeq a'$ gives $[U_0a_n']^{-1}[U_0k_n]=[U_0a_n]^{-1}$. Together with $[\operatorname{pr}_n^{J'}][\lim l]=[l_n][\operatorname{pr}_n^J]$, these show that the normalized projection $[U_0a_n]^{-1}[j_n]^{-1}[\operatorname{pr}_n^J]$ commutes with the resolution transitions. The other side of step 4 commutes by the same first-resolution equation and naturality of $\operatorname{pr}_n^{U_0I}$. These are precisely the two sides of the asserted equality. Uniqueness of the homotopy classes in step 5 gives identity and composition compatibility, including a change of $j$ alone by taking $k=1$.

lean.statement: theorem acyclicity {N I : CochainComplex (StrictRingSystem B) ℤ} (a : N ⟶ I) [QuasiIso a] [I.IsKInjective] {T : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Modules A) ℤ} (j : (restrictionComplex A B α).obj I ⟶ T) [QuasiIso j] [T.IsKInjective] : QuasiIso ((limitComplex A).map j) ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso (componentMap A ((restrictionComplex A B α).map a) n) ∧ QuasiIso (componentMap A j n) ∧ ∃ (ea : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (((restrictionComplex A B α).obj N).asFunctor.obj (op n)) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (((restrictionComplex A B α).obj I).asFunctor.obj (op n))) (ej : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (((restrictionComplex A B α).obj I).asFunctor.obj (op n)) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.asFunctor.obj (op n))), ea.hom = DerivedCategory.Q.map (componentMap A ((restrictionComplex A B α).map a) n) ∧ ej.hom = DerivedCategory.Q.map (componentMap A j n) ∧ DerivedCategory.Q.map ((limitComplex A).map j) ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (projection A T n) ≫ ej.inv ≫ ea.inv = DerivedCategory.Q.map (projection A ((restrictionComplex A B α).obj I) n) ≫ ea.inv
